scenes.heading: REST
scenes.caption: REST is a style of API that uses URLs as nouns and HTTP methods as verbs. GET reads, POST creates, PUT or PATCH updates, DELETE removes. It is the style most web backends speak, so teams can guess the shape of a new endpoint.

scenes.caption: GraphQL is an API style where the client names the fields it wants, and the server answers with just those fields, in one request. It avoids a pile of endpoints that each return too much. It requires the server to define a schema and to think about the cost of nested queries.

scenes.heading: JWT
scenes.caption: A JWT is a signed token that carries claims, such as a user id and an expiry. Anyone can read the payload. Only the signer can produce a signature that checks out. Servers like them because they can check the signature without a database lookup. The cost is that you cannot easily take one back before it expires.

scenes.heading: Rate limiting
scenes.caption: Rate limiting caps how many requests a caller may make in a window of time. Past the cap, you refuse with a clear status and a hint about when to retry. It protects the service from a bug, a loop, or an attacker. It also protects a single client from accidentally melting their own quota.
